method: Bounded public-web search and direct metadata review of Reuters, Associated Press, BBC, and Guardian publication surfaces. Only stable canonical article URLs with verifiable in-window publication times were admitted. No authentication, paywall or robots bypass, full-text capture, binary download, inferred timestamp, map capture, or precise operational-location retention was used.

sources_checked.result: Reuters exposed a stable article URL and displayed publication time of 08:35 UTC on 5 August 2026 for the EU frozen-assets support item. Earlier Reuters records from the completed 00:00–05:00 UTC interval were not duplicated.

The Guardian exposed stable publication metadata for a Leipzig security analysis at 17:32 UTC. The Kyiv air-defence article was excluded because its canonical URL is already represented by item_20260805_guardian_air_defence_criticism in another shard; the current page's displayed first-publication time differs from that existing record and remains unresolved metadata drift rather than a second identity.
A stable AP article URL and 5 August dateline were available, but the approved parsed page did not expose an exact publication timestamp. It was not admitted by date inference.
Candidate article pages were not retrievable through the approved public-web connector because of robots restrictions; no bypass was attempted.

included_items.short_excerpt_original: EU to use €1.4 billion from interest on frozen Russian assets to help Ukraine
included_items.quote_locator: Reuters article heading and displayed publication metadata.
included_items.summary: Reuters reported an EU announcement that €1.4 billion from interest on frozen Russian assets would be made available to support Ukraine.
included_items.lineage_note: The article attributes the announcement to the European Commission and quotes its president; the Commission primary statement was not separately registered in this media shard.

included_items.short_excerpt_original: The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe
included_items.quote_locator: Guardian analysis heading and publication line.
included_items.summary: The Guardian published a labelled analysis of the security implications of an explosive-bearing drone found near Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig airport.
included_items.publication_time_basis: The Guardian displayed publication at 19:32 CEST on 5 August 2026 and last modification at 04:18 CEST on 6 August 2026; these convert to 17:32 and 02:18 UTC.
included_items.lineage_note: The analysis cites German police, German media, NATO context, and expert interpretation. Attribution about possible state involvement remains the publication's analysis and was not independently assessed here.

access_failures.detail: Robots restrictions prevented retrieval through the approved connector. No alternate bypass, cached full-text source, or authentication was used.
The parsed page exposed the article, author, dateline, and event date but not an exact publication timestamp suitable for the task window.

The current page's first-publication line differs from the timestamp stored by the existing canonical source item. No immutable earlier page bytes or complete revision history were available to resolve the drift.
Reuters and Guardian pages were reviewed as current public pages. No immutable webpage bytes, content hashes, or complete revision histories were captured.

artifact_capture.reason: No full article text, image, video, map, page bytes, or other immutable artifact was downloaded, hashed, or stored.

coverage_gaps: The bounded result contains two new publications from two outlets and is not an exhaustive survey of international media coverage.
The AP candidate was excluded because exact publication time could not be verified; BBC candidate pages were blocked by robots restrictions.
The existing Guardian Kyiv canonical record and the current page expose conflicting publication-time metadata that could not be resolved without an immutable earlier version.
The Guardian Leipzig analysis was modified after the task window, so the retained metadata distinguishes first publication from later modification but does not preserve the original page version.
The admitted articles aggregate official statements, wire reporting, witnesses, and analysis whose complete upstream canonical lineage was not separately registered.
No full text, images, video, maps, or immutable webpage artifacts were captured.
No media assertion was independently assessed or converted into a claim, observation, territorial conclusion, or report narrative.
safety_notes: No precise current positions, movement routes, active-unit locations, target coordinates, vulnerable-facility details, or map geometry were persisted.
No copyrighted article body or binary media was stored.
All casualty, responsibility, and security-attribution language remains explicitly attributed to the publications and their named upstreams.
